visualReview.notes: Inspected the whole-model turntable and detail renders. All four openings have a clear silhouette with separated piers, molded raised base, domed canopy and finial. The original stylized figure is visible through the four openings and reads from the main west viewpoint.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the current shared-material images and unload result. The molded pale concrete, deeper stone trim, brass accent and bronze figure read as distinct surfaces. The canopy does not obscure the west-facing figure at normal ground eye height.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected the 25 current contextual frames and detail-level comparisons. The square high base, four open arches and dome persist at all levels. Closer levels add curved arch trim, pilaster bands, molded plinth corners and details of the bronze figure.

geographicReview.notes: The exact named mapped perimeter and documented orientation toward Bhimarn Prathom fix the plan and facing. The original independent 256 m heightfield and unmasked terrain render were inspected. The plinth contacts the gently varying lawn and its depth remains approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Standing Thewalai Khanet in Sanam Chandra Palace, including its tall shaped concrete platform, open four-sided pavilion, domed canopy, crown finial and simplified bronze Ganesha figure facing Bhimarn Prathom.
fidelityReview.notes: The conservation study describes the raised platform, concrete domed canopy and brass ornament. The Fine Arts Department inventory and historical research identify the enclosed figure and ceremonial axis. Heights, exact decorative motif and the rendered bronze figure’s proportions are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Reviewed the story’s Qualla imagery first. The native Qualla photograph of this shrine requires attribution and was excluded. The model is an original reconstruction from the measured footprint and primary written records.

primaryFactsReview.notes: The exact mapped footprint and written site records support the raised concrete platform, open domed shrine and bronze figure. Doorhood, ornament, figure details and section heights are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing Thewalai Khanet shrine at Sanam Chandra Palace, including its molded pedestal, four open arches, domed canopy and bronze figure.

limitations: The mapped shrine perimeter and west facing axis are retained. Section heights, local footing, access dimensions and canopy curvature are estimated.
Canopy profile, platform ornament and the character of the open portals follow architectural descriptions. Exact sculptural motifs, relief, finish colors and hidden surfaces are inferred.
The small bronze figure is a simplified original rendering from textual identification, materials and facing. Its individual iconographic details are approximate.
The original terrain is used at the mapped lawn and no ground shaping is authored.
